$schema_note: Payment Services Regulations 2017 (SI 2017/752), regulation 76 and the provisions it depends on. Derived from the XML at legislation.gov.uk, digests in source/PROVENANCE.md. Decomposed WITHOUT consulting the Banxico clause register; primitive attribution was made afterwards, against banxico-34-2010/primitives.json.
$reuse_classification_withdrawn: Each clause used to carry `primitive` and `reuse` fields, one primitive per clause, written by hand. Withdrawn 2026-08-21. THE 86% REUSE FIGURE IN FINDINGS.md WAS COMPUTED BY COUNTING THESE FIELDS, which made a hand-authored classification read as a measurement. An execution trace of both evaluators (see ../_primitives/INVENTORY-AUDIT.md) found the `primitive` field names the sole top-level call on 13 of 21 clauses and disagrees on 8: five clauses invoke more primitives than the field recorded, and three declare one that no fixture reaches. `reuse_note` is kept, because it carries authorial reasoning about WHY a shape transferred, which no trace can recover; it is prose and was never a measurement.
$what_derives_it_now: NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY. The audit's tracer instruments both evaluators and attributes calls to clauses by depth, but it lives in a scratchpad and was not committed, so this repo contains no instrument that derives which primitives a clause invokes. `check-coverage.mjs` derives the clause id SET from a live run and is unaffected by this withdrawal; it never read these fields. No deriver is being invented here to replace them.
scope_note: Boundary set by the source. Reg 76 is `subject to regulations 74 and 75` and turns on whether a transaction was authorised `in accordance with regulation 67`, so 74, 75 and 67 are in. Regulation 72 is referenced BY 75(3) and 75(4) as the subject of a proof burden, two hops from 76 and never as a condition of the refund, so it is excluded and named here rather than silently dropped. Section 333A(2) of the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 is external primary legislation, not part of this instrument.

clauses.text_en: A payment transaction is authorised only if the payer has given consent to that transaction or to a series of which it forms part.
clauses.reuse_note: Two alternatives under 67(1)(a) and (b), EITHER OF WHICH SATISFIES UNLESS THE SERIES LIMB IS DEFEATED. This clause reads psr-2017/67/4/series-withdrawal: a series whose consent was withdrawn before the transaction does not authorise it, and where the ordering cannot be established this returns `undetermined`.
clauses.$finding_2026_08_23:
BASIS IS NOW FALSE, AND I MADE IT SO THIS SESSION. Reported, NOT rewritten, on the brief's stop condition. `reuse_note` reads `Two alternatives, either of which satisfies: consent to the transaction, or consent to a series.` That was true until reg 67(4) was given effect on 2026-08-23. It is now false: series consent alone does NOT satisfy where the series was withdrawn before the transaction, and this clause reads psr-2017/67/4/series-withdrawal to find out.

I changed the behaviour and left the sentence describing the old one, which is the same defect this session found three times in other people's clauses and once in a second copy of my own correction. Found by check-claimed-effects.mjs, which reported it as read-but-not-claimed.
clauses.$corrected_2026_08_23:
WAS: `Two alternatives, either of which satisfies: consent to the transaction, or consent to a series. Exactly the shape inciso d) needed.` That was true until 2026-08-23 AND I AM THE ONE WHO MADE IT FALSE, by giving reg 67(4) effect earlier the same day and leaving the sentence describing the behaviour I had just replaced.

It is the same defect this session found three times in clauses I did not write, and once in a second copy of my own correction. FOUND BY check-claimed-effects.mjs, NOT BY READING: the note is plausible, it is the field a reader would look at, and nothing about it looks stale.

clauses.text_en: Consent must be given in the form and in accordance with the procedure agreed between payer and provider.
clauses.reuse_note: The agreed forms are an institutional register, exactly as the authorised signatory list was.

clauses.text_en: Consent may be given before execution, or after execution if that is agreed between payer and provider.
clauses.reuse_note: Post-execution consent is permitted only where the precondition, an agreement to that effect, holds.

clauses.text_en: The payer may withdraw consent at any time before the point at which the payment order can no longer be revoked under regulation 83.
clauses.reuse_note: NEW. Compares two instants for order with no limit. elapsed_within measures an interval AGAINST A LIMIT and cannot express `before` without inventing one.

clauses.text_en: Subject to regulation 83(3) to (5), the payer may withdraw its consent to the execution of a series of payment transactions at any time with the effect that any future payment transactions are not regarded as authorised for the purposes of this Part.
clauses.reuse_note: Reads no fact of its own; changes the authorisation result for later transactions.
clauses.$corrected_2026_08_23:
WAS `DERIVED`, on the basis `Reads no fact of its own; changes the authorisation result for later transactions.` BOTH HALVES ARE FALSE AGAINST THE CODE, and the disposition was wrong rather than just the sentence.

FIRST HALF. The evaluator reads `f.consent?.series_withdrawn_at` directly at evaluate.mjs:175. A clause that reads a fact is not DERIVED, whose definition in this estate is `decides nothing directly; composes other results`. Its observed result domain is {not_satisfied, not_applicable}, which is the applicability signature, so CONDITIONAL is the disposition: the consequence arises only where a withdrawal is recorded.

SECOND HALF, AND IT IS A LIVE DEFECT RATHER THAN A WRONG SENTENCE. Measured 2026-08-23: withdrawing a series changes nothing. `psr-2017/67/1/consent` computes `any_present([to_transaction, to_series])` and never consults the withdrawal, so a series whose consent has been withdrawn still returns `one_present` and `psr-2017/76/1/trigger` is unchanged. THIS CLAUSE'S RESULT IS CONSUMED BY NOTHING. The encoding states reg 67(4) and does not give it effect.

NOT FIXED HERE. Correcting the disposition is a register correction; making the withdrawal reach the authorisation result is a substantive change to a rule in a register that is public on main, and it is a ruling rather than a tidy-up. Reported.
clauses.$fixed_2026_08_23:
GIVEN EFFECT. The clause is now consumed by psr-2017/67/1/consent, which it defeats for transactions FUTURE to the withdrawal. Before this it emitted a result nothing read, so the encoding stated reg 67(4) and did not apply it.

HOW IT WAS FOUND. By TRACING which clause results are consumed, not by reading the register. The register's own basis said the clause `changes the authorisation result for later transactions`, which is an assertion about an effect it did not have, and no check tested it. A stated effect is not a control.

THE READING IS THE TEXT'S. `any future payment transactions` is relative to the withdrawal, so the operation is an ordering and not a presence test: a transaction executed BEFORE the withdrawal keeps its series consent.

STATED LIMITATION. 67(4) opens `Subject to regulation 83(3) to (5)`, which bounds when a withdrawal is EFFECTIVE. Regulation 83 is two hops from reg 76 and outside this encoding's scope, so a recorded withdrawal is treated as an effective one. That is an assumption about availability, not about effect.

NO WORKED CASE MOVED. All three fixtures carry `series_withdrawn_at: null`, so none reaches the corrected path. The behaviour changed and the suite did not, which is the same shape as every other defect found here.

clauses.text_en: The user must notify the provider without undue delay on becoming aware of the unauthorised transaction.
clauses.reuse_note: `without undue delay` is a qualitative standard with no test in the source, the same shape as `lenguaje simple y claro`.

clauses.text_en: Entitlement to redress arises only if notification is given no later than 13 months after the debit date.
clauses.reuse_note: Same primitive, new unit. Banxico needed calendar_days and business_days; this needs months, which is not a fixed multiple of either.

clauses.text_en: The 13 month bar does not apply where the provider failed to supply the Part 6 information about the transaction.
clauses.reuse_note: A disapplication rather than an obligation, expressed by negating the precondition. No new shape.

clauses.text_en: Where the user denies authorising a transaction, the provider must prove it was authenticated, accurately recorded, entered in its accounts and unaffected by technical breakdown or other deficiency.
clauses.reuse_note: Four conjuncts, each a held assessment. The conjunction is composed; the conjuncts are judgments.
clauses.evidential_role: allocates the burden of proving the reg 67 question to the provider
clauses.$recategorised_2026_08_23: WAS JUDGMENT. EVIDENTIAL, on the 2026-08-23 ruling: reg 75 governs how reg 76(1)'s only condition is ANSWERED when the user denies authorisation, not whether the refund duty holds. Its result is an input to the clause named in `governs`, not a determination of its own, and it is NOT a conjunct of psr-2017/76/1/trigger. See ../_primitives/EVIDENTIAL.md.

clauses.text_en: Where a payment initiation service provider was involved, it must prove the same matters within its sphere of competence.
clauses.reuse_note: Same standard, different bearer.
clauses.evidential_role: allocates the same burden to a payment initiation service provider, within its sphere of competence
clauses.$recategorised_2026_08_23: WAS JUDGMENT. EVIDENTIAL, on the 2026-08-23 ruling: reg 75 governs how reg 76(1)'s only condition is ANSWERED when the user denies authorisation, not whether the refund duty holds. Its result is an input to the clause named in `governs`, not a determination of its own, and it is NOT a conjunct of psr-2017/76/1/trigger. See ../_primitives/EVIDENTIAL.md.

clauses.text_en: The recorded use of a payment instrument is not in itself necessarily sufficient to prove that the payer authorised the transaction or acted fraudulently or with gross negligence.
clauses.reuse_note: THE SAME SHAPE AS `por lo menos`, at arity one. Banxico's floor said a complete element list does not establish conformance; this says one item of evidence does not establish authorisation. Both forbid reading necessary as sufficient. Parameterised because the existing signature takes a list.
clauses.evidential_role: bounds what the recorded use of an instrument suffices to prove
clauses.$recategorised_2026_08_23: WAS DERIVED. EVIDENTIAL, on the 2026-08-23 ruling: reg 75 governs how reg 76(1)'s only condition is ANSWERED when the user denies authorisation, not whether the refund duty holds. Its result is an input to the clause named in `governs`, not a determination of its own, and it is NOT a conjunct of psr-2017/76/1/trigger. See ../_primitives/EVIDENTIAL.md.

clauses.text_en: A provider claiming the payer acted fraudulently or with gross negligence must provide supporting evidence to the payer.
clauses.reuse_note: The obligation arises only on the claim being made.
clauses.evidential_role: requires disclosure of supporting evidence to the payer
clauses.$recategorised_2026_08_23: WAS CONDITIONAL. EVIDENTIAL, on the 2026-08-23 ruling: reg 75 governs how reg 76(1)'s only condition is ANSWERED when the user denies authorisation, not whether the refund duty holds. Its result is an input to the clause named in `governs`, not a determination of its own, and it is NOT a conjunct of psr-2017/76/1/trigger. See ../_primitives/EVIDENTIAL.md.

clauses.text_en: Subject to regulations 74 and 75, where an executed transaction was not authorised under regulation 67, the provider must refund and restore.
clauses.reuse_note: Composes the 67 authorisation result with the 74 bar. Reads no fact directly.
clauses.disposition_basis: Composes the 67 authorisation result with the 74 bar. Reads no fact directly.
clauses.$corrected_2026_08_23:
WAS: `Composes the 67 authorisation result with the 74 bar and the 75 burden. Reads no fact directly.` THE `75 BURDEN` CLAUSE OF THAT SENTENCE WAS FALSE: traced, this clause reads `psr-2017/75/1/provider-burden` ZERO TIMES.

RULED 2026-08-23 THAT THE ENCODING IS RIGHT AND THE SENTENCE WAS WRONG. Reg 76(1) turns on one substantive condition, that the transaction was not authorised in accordance with reg 67, and is `Subject to regulations 74 and 75`. Reg 74 bars the remedy on time. REG 75 ALLOCATES THE BURDEN OF PROVING THE REG 67 QUESTION when the user denies authorisation; it determines how that condition is ANSWERED, not whether the duty holds. So it is not a conjunct of this trigger.

FOUND BY TRACING, NOT DECLARED. Nothing compared the basis against the code, and the basis had been read as a description of the encoding for as long as it existed. This is the second false effect claim found this way, after psr-2017/67/4, and the third counting 34-2010/3.6/p5/foreign-deadline.

SECOND COPY, FOUND BY check-claimed-effects.mjs ON ITS FIRST REAL RUN. The false sentence lived in TWO fields, `disposition_basis` and `reuse_note`, and the correction above changed only the first. `reuse_note` still read: `Composes the 67 authorisation result with the 74 bar and the 75 burden. Reads no fact directly.` Corrected now. A correction applied to one of two copies is the defect this estate has recorded before, and it is exactly what a check comparing prose to a live run is for: reading the register would not have shown it, because the corrected field was the one a reader would look at.

clauses.text_en: The provider must refund the amount of the unauthorised transaction to the payer.
clauses.reuse_note: NEW. Requires comparing two scaled monetary values for EQUALITY. The existing set has no numeric comparison at all: Banxico's ceiling test lived inside the engine's mandate evaluator and was never lifted into a primitive.

clauses.text_en: Where applicable, the provider must restore the debited account to the state it would have been in had the transaction not taken place.
clauses.reuse_note: `where applicable` is the precondition. The restored state itself is a held assessment, since it is a counterfactual.

clauses.text_en: The refund must be provided as soon as practicable.
clauses.reuse_note: A second standard sitting on the same sentence as a hard deadline. They fail independently.

clauses.text_en: In any event the refund must be provided no later than the end of the business day following the day on which the provider becomes aware of the unauthorised transaction.
clauses.reuse_note: business_days already existed as a unit. Unchanged.

clauses.text_en: The deadline does not apply where the provider has reasonable grounds to suspect fraudulent behaviour by the user and notifies a person mentioned in section 333A(2) of the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 in writing.
clauses.reuse_note: A carve-out whose precondition is itself a conjunction of a judgment and a recorded act.

clauses.text_en: When crediting the account, the credit value date must be no later than the date on which the amount was debited.
clauses.reuse_note: Second user of the same new shape. Two instants, no limit. This is why it is recorded as a shape rather than a one-off.

clauses.text_en: Where the transaction was initiated through a payment initiation service provider, the account servicing provider must still comply with paragraph (1).
clauses.reuse_note: Routes the paragraph (1) result to a different bearer.

clauses.text_en: Where the payment initiation service provider is liable under regulation 75(2), it must compensate the account servicing provider immediately on request.
clauses.reuse_note: Two preconditions, liability and a request.

$dispositions: MECHANICAL, JUDGMENT, CONDITIONAL, DERIVED, EVIDENTIAL. See ../_primitives/EVIDENTIAL.md for the last.
